problems.title: Multiply powers in a monomial
problems.question: Write $-(-\frac23p^2q^4)^3(-3pq^2)^2$ in standard form.
problems.idea: Handle the coefficient, sign and each variable separately.
formulas: $(uv)^n=u^nv^n$; $(x^m)^n=x^{mn}$; $x^rx^s=x^{r+s}$.
steps: The cubed factor is -(8/27)p⁶q¹²; the minus sign outside makes it +(8/27)p⁶q¹².
The squared factor is 9p²q⁴.
Multiply coefficients: (8/27)·9=8/3, and add variable exponents.

problems.title: Pair reciprocal bases
problems.question: Evaluate $(5/7)^{10}\cdot1.4^9\cdot7^2$.
problems.idea: The decimal 1.4 equals the reciprocal 7/5.
formulas: aⁿ·a⁻ᵐ=aⁿ⁻ᵐ.
steps: Nine copies of 5/7 cancel nine copies of 7/5, leaving 5/7.

problems.title: Opposite sides identify a parallelogram
problems.question: A quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Which equality must hold?
problems.idea: Use the basic property of a parallelogram.
formulas: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal.
steps: The parallel-side condition defines a parallelogram.
A diagonal splits it into two congruent triangles, using alternate interior angles and the shared diagonal.
Hence corresponding opposite sides AB and CD are equal.

problems.title: An upstream and downstream round trip
problems.question: A boat’s speed in still water is 8 km/h and the current is 2 km/h. It must go upstream and return within 4 hours. Find its maximum upstream distance.
problems.idea: The same distance is covered at two different speeds.
formulas: Time=distance/speed; upstream speed=u-v, downstream speed=u+v.
steps: The upstream and downstream speeds are 6 and 10 km/h.
For distance d, total time is d/6+d/10=4d/15.
The greatest distance uses all 4 hours: 4d/15=4, hence d=15.

problems.title: Separate two questions printed together
problems.question: ABC is equilateral. ACD is isosceles with angle ADC=40°; B,D lie on the same side of AC. AD crosses BC at O. The source asks for both ABD and COD.
problems.idea: Use symmetry about the perpendicular bisector of AC, then triangle angles.
formulas: An isosceles triangle has equal base angles; an equilateral triangle has 60° angles.
steps: If AD=CD, the base angles at A,C of ACD are 70°. B,D lie on the same perpendicular bisector of AC, with D above B. Hence ABD=150°.
In that case triangle AOC has angles 70° at A and 60° at C, so AOC=50°. The opposite ray OD gives COD=130°.
If instead AC=CD, angles CAD and ADC are 40° and ACD=100°. Then BCD=100°-60°=40°, and BC=CD makes CBD=70°. Thus ABD=60°+70°=130°.
In this second configuration AOC=180°-40°-60°=80°, giving COD=100°. Both configurations allow the stated crossing.
problems.answer: If AD=CD: ABD=150°, COD=130°. If AC=CD: ABD=130°, COD=100°.
problems.note: The question does not specify the equal sides of ACD and prints two angle requests. Both sets above are compatible with its stated geometry; a unique answer needs a named base or diagram.

problems.title: Extend a median by its own length
problems.question: AD is a median of ABC and is extended to E with DE=AD. Triangle ABD has perimeter 5, and AD+DC=4.2. Find CE.
problems.idea: The diagonals of ABEC bisect each other.
formulas: A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a parallelogram.
steps: Because AD=DE and BD=DC, D is the midpoint of both AE and BC.
Therefore ABEC is a parallelogram and CE=AB.
The perimeter gives AB+BD+AD=5. Since BD+AD=DC+AD=4.2, AB=0.8.

problems.title: Clear fractional coefficients
problems.question: Solve $2-\frac{3x-7}{4}+\frac{x+17}{5}=0$.
problems.idea: Multiply every term by the common denominator 20.
formulas: Multiplying an equation by a nonzero constant preserves its solutions.
steps: Multiplication gives 40-5(3x-7)+4(x+17)=0.

problems.title: A median from two perimeters
problems.question: ABC is isosceles with base AC and median BD. Its perimeter is 48; triangle BCD has perimeter 36. Find BD.
problems.idea: Half of the original perimeter equals BC+CD.
formulas: In an isosceles triangle AB=BC, and a median to AC gives CD=AC/2.
steps: The large perimeter is 2BC+AC=48.
Divide by 2: BC+CD=24.
The small perimeter is BC+CD+BD=36, so BD=36-24=12.

problems.title: An incenter angle determines a vertex angle
problems.question: The obtuse angle between the internal bisectors at A and B is five times angle C. Find C.
problems.idea: Use the incenter angle theorem.
formulas: $\angle AIB=90^\circ+C/2$.
steps: The equation is 90°+C/2=5C.
Divide to obtain C=20°.

problems.title: Angle between two altitudes
problems.question: Two angles of a triangle are 68° and 52°. Find the acute angle between the altitudes from those vertices.
problems.idea: Rotating two lines by 90° preserves the acute angle between them.
formulas: Triangle angles sum to 180°; altitudes are perpendicular to the opposite sides.
steps: The third angle is 180°-68°-52°=60°.
The two altitudes are perpendicular to the sides that enclose that third angle.
Their line angles are 60° and 120°; the acute one is 60°.

problems.title: Dry matter stays constant
problems.question: Fresh apples contain 90% water; dried apples contain 10% water. How much fresh fruit gives 10 kg of dried fruit?
problems.idea: Only water is removed, so the dry matter has the same mass.
formulas: Dry mass=total mass·(1-water fraction).
steps: The dried fruit contains 10·0.9=9 kg of dry matter.
Fresh apples are 10% dry matter. If their mass is M, then 0.1M=9.
Hence M=90.

problems.title: Recover the whole journey
problems.question: A traveller covers 3/8 of the route on day one and 25 km on day two. Together these equal half the route. Find its length.
problems.idea: Subtract the fractions of the total route.
steps: The second day represents 1/8 of the entire route.
Therefore L/8=25.
Multiply by 8 to get L=200.

problems.title: Remove a shared internal side
problems.question: An equilateral triangle ABC has perimeter 24. A triangle ACD on the other side of AC has perimeter 20. Find the outer quadrilateral’s perimeter.
problems.idea: Adding the triangle perimeters counts the internal side AC twice.
formulas: Outer perimeter=P₁+P₂-2·shared side.
steps: Each equilateral side is 24/3=8, so AC=8.
The combined perimeters total 44.
Remove the two copies of AC: 44-16=28.

problems.title: Repeated replacement of a mixture
problems.question: A barrel has 32 L of pure alcohol. Remove 8 L and replace with water; repeat this operation three times in total. How much alcohol remains?
problems.idea: Each well-mixed removal leaves the same fraction of alcohol.
formulas: Remaining alcohol after n replacements=initial alcohol·(1-removed volume/total volume)ⁿ.
steps: Each replacement leaves 1-8/32=3/4 of the alcohol.
After three operations the amount is 32(3/4)³.
This equals 32·27/64=13.5.

problems.title: Which notable triangle point is it?
problems.question: ABC is isosceles with AB=AC. AA₁ is an altitude and BB₁ is a median. Identify their intersection.
problems.idea: The altitude from the apex of an isosceles triangle is also a median.
formulas: The medians of a triangle meet at its centroid.
steps: Because AB=AC, the perpendicular from A to BC bisects BC.
Thus AA₁ and BB₁ are both medians.
Their intersection is the centroid; it need not be all the other triangle centres.

problems.title: Dilute a syrup
problems.question: How much water must be added to 20 L of 12% syrup to make 10% syrup?
problems.idea: The amount of dissolved substance stays unchanged.
formulas: Concentration=solute volume/total solution volume.
steps: The solute amount is 20·0.12=2.4 L in the model.
At 10%, the required total is 2.4/0.10=24 L.
Add 24-20=4 L of water.

problems.title: Expand both sides of a decimal equation
problems.question: Solve 0.2(x-1.4)+1.2=1.4(2x-1)-0.8.
problems.idea: Collect the variable terms on one side and constants on the other.
formulas: Distributive law: a(b+c)=ab+ac.
steps: The left side is 0.2x+0.92; the right side is 2.8x-2.2.
Dividing gives x=1.2.

problems.title: Degree of a product of monomials
problems.question: Find the degree of $(2a^2bc^4)^3(-0.5ab^2)^2$.
problems.idea: Add the exponents after simplifying the powers.
formulas: The degree of a monomial is the sum of its variable exponents.
steps: The first factor is 8a⁶b³c¹²; the second is 0.25a²b⁴.
Their product is 2a⁸b⁷c¹².
Its degree is 8+7+12=27.

problems.title: Altitude and bisector from one vertex
problems.question: In a triangle B=3C. The angle between the altitude and internal angle bisector from A is 25°. Find all angles.
problems.idea: The angle between these two lines is half the difference of the base angles.
formulas: Angle between the altitude and bisector from A=|B-C|/2.
steps: Substitute B=3C: |B-C|/2=2C/2=C.
Thus C=25° and B=75°.

problems.title: Prime and even integer bounds
problems.question: Add the smallest prime greater than 71.2 to the greatest even integer less than 3.27.
problems.idea: Check the nearest integers satisfying each condition.
formulas: A prime has exactly two positive divisors; an even integer is divisible by 2.
steps: 72 is composite, while 73 has no prime divisor up to √73, so it is prime.
The greatest even integer below 3.27 is 2.
Their sum is 73+2=75.

problems.title: Converse of the hypotenuse median theorem
problems.question: The median to AC in triangle ABC equals AC/2. What kind of angle is B?
problems.idea: The midpoint of AC is equally far from A,B,C.
formulas: A triangle inscribed in a circle with a diameter as one side has a right angle opposite that side.
steps: Let M be the midpoint of AC. Then MA=MC=AC/2 and the given median BM has that same length.
A,B,C lie on the circle centred at M, and AC is its diameter.
By the angle-in-a-semicircle theorem, angle B=90°.

problems.title: Father and son ages
problems.question: A father and son have combined age a. In three years the father will be twice the son’s age. Find the son’s current age.
problems.idea: Write both conditions using current ages F,S.
formulas: After three years the ages are F+3 and S+3.
steps: F+S=a and F+3=2(S+3).
The second equation simplifies to F=2S+3.
Substitute into the first: 3S+3=a, giving S=(a-3)/3.

problems.title: Union minus intersection
problems.question: A is the prime divisors of 66, and B is the positive odd integers below 20. Find |A∪B|-|A∩B|.
problems.idea: List the small sets explicitly.
steps: Their intersection is {3,11}, with 2 elements.
The union has 3+10-2=11 elements, so the requested difference is 11-2=9.

problems.title: When squaring fails to increase a number
problems.question: For which real a is a<a² false?
problems.idea: Negate the strict inequality, then factor.
formulas: a≥a² is equivalent to a(a-1)≤0.
steps: The inequality is false when a≥a².
The product a(a-1) is nonpositive exactly between its roots 0 and 1, including both.
At either endpoint there is equality, so the original strict inequality is indeed false.

problems.title: An identity in the unknown x
problems.question: For which a does (a-1)(a-2)x=(a-2)(a-3) have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Both the coefficient of x and the constant side must be zero.
formulas: Ax=B has infinitely many solutions iff A=0 and B=0.
steps: The coefficient vanishes at a=1 or a=2.
The right side vanishes at a=2 or a=3.
Only a=2 satisfies both requirements.
